newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung backs China's plan to revise textbooks.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung backs China's plan to revise textbooks.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Tuesday threw his support behind China's proposal to rewrite parts of school textbooks after the British colony is returned to Beijing later this year.
"There are areas where textbooks need to be rewritten...and other issues which refer to the colonial past that need to be looked at," Tung said at a news conference.

Possible changes include not only simple references to China -- which in future will become a "sovereign" instead of the current "neighbouring country" -- but also those describing sensitive issues like the 19th century opium wars, Tung said.
Britain prised Hong Kong from China a century and a half ago through the gunboat diplomacy and so-called opium wars that were sparked over opium that Western traders were shipping to China.

"The opium wars are referred to as a dispute of trade...all these things need to be reviewed very very carefully," Tung said, citing one example of events that Chinese felt were glossed over or omitted in present textbooks.
On Monday, colonial Governor Chris Patten lashed out at Beijing after Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said school books should be revised.
